10 exercises · B1 – C1

How to use this book

Har bir mashq — 8 qadam. Bir mashq ≈ 2 dars.

🗺️
📩
1. Read the situation

Read the email or letter and the three tasks.

Vaziyat va uchta topshiriqni diqqat bilan o‘qing.

🔍
2. Read & think

Answer 4 quick questions about the message.

Xat bo‘yicha 4 ta savolga javob bering.

🔤
3. Word power

Match the key words with their Uzbek meaning.

Kalit so‘zlarni o‘zbekcha ma’nosi bilan moslang.

🎭
4. Formal or informal?

Decide which phrases belong in which letter.

Iboralar qaysi xatga mosligini aniqlang.

🧠
5. Plan it

Make quick notes for every task before you write.

Yozishdan oldin har bir topshiriq uchun reja tuzing.

✍️
6. Write

Write Task 1.1, Task 1.2 and Part 2. Count your words and tick the checklist.

Uchala topshiriqni yozing, so‘zlarni sanang.

⭐
7. Model answers

Compare with the model letters. Highlighted words are worth learning.

Namunaviy javoblar bilan solishtiring.

🔗
8. Linkers & words

Complete the model blog post with linkers, then learn the word list.

Bog‘lovchilarni qo‘ying va lug‘atni yodlang.

💡 Tip: Time yourself like in the real exam — about 60 minutes for all three tasks: ≈ 10 min for Task 1.1, ≈ 20 min for Task 1.2 and ≈ 30 min for Part 2. Use the score tracker to see your progress.
Multilevel · Yozma ish

The writing exam

Tuzilma, talablar va baholash mezonlari

📝

Chet tilidan yozma ish topshiriqlari nomzodning til bilimini kompleks baholashga qaratilgan. Ushbu topshiriqlar orqali quyidagi ko‘nikmalar aniqlanadi:

grammatik bilimso‘z boyligifikrni mantiqiy va izchil ifodalashuslubiy moslikkommunikativ kompetensiya
B1–B2

1-bo‘lim: Elektron xatlar

✉️

Nomzod bitta vaziyat asosida ikki xil elektron xat (email) yozadi.

B1≈ 50 so‘z

Task 1.1 · Norasmiy xat (do‘stga)

Uslub: oddiy, samimiy · Maqsad: shaxsiy fikr, hissiyot va rejalarni bildirish

  • sodda va tushunarli gaplar
  • kundalik leksika
  • fikrlar orasidagi mantiqiy bog‘lanish
B2120–150 so‘z

Task 1.2 · Rasmiy xat (tashkilot yoki rahbariyatga)

Uslub: rasmiy · Maqsad: muammo, taklif, shikoyat yoki so‘rov bildirish

  • rasmiy uslubga mos leksika
  • murakkab grammatik tuzilmalar
  • mantiqiy izchillik (coherence)
  • bog‘lovchi vositalardan to‘g‘ri foydalanish (cohesion)
Muhim jihat: Nomzod bir xil vaziyatni ikki xil uslubda ifodalay olishi kerak. Bu uning tilni real hayotiy vaziyatlarda samarali qo‘llay olish qobiliyatini ko‘rsatadi.
C1

2-bo‘lim: Blog posti yoki maqola

💻

Nomzod umumiy qiziqish uyg‘otadigan mavzu asosida ijodiy-tahliliy matn yozadi.

C1180–200 so‘z

Baholash mezonlari

  • 3–4 ball — B1/B2 darajaga mos javob
  • 5 ball — yuqori darajadagi yozma ish

  • 6 ball — C1 dan yuqori daraja

Xulosa: Yozma ish topshiriqlari — bu faqat grammatik test emas, balki nomzodning fikrlash darajasi, kommunikativ qobiliyati va tilni real vaziyatda qo‘llash ko‘nikmasini aniqlashga xizmat qiluvchi muhim baholash vositasidir.
Muvaffaqiyatli yozma ish uchun: vaziyatni to‘g‘ri tushunishuslubni to‘g‘ri tanlashfikrni mantiqiy bayon qilishboy leksika va to‘g‘ri grammatikadan foydalanish
Your writing toolkit

Phrase bank

Informal vs formal · Blog post plan · Linkers

🧰

😊 Informal (Task 1.1)

Start

  • Hi Jack, / Hey Sam,
  • How are you doing?
  • Did you hear about …?
  • Guess what!

Feelings

  • I'm so excited about …
  • I'm a bit gutted / upset that …
  • Honestly, it's really annoying.
  • I can't wait!

Ideas

  • Maybe we could …
  • Why don't we …?
  • I think they should …
  • How about …?

Finish

  • Let me know what you think!
  • Talk soon, / Take care,
  • See you soon,
  • Best, + your name

🎩 Formal (Task 1.2)

Start

  • Dear Mr Smith, / Dear Manager,
  • I am writing regarding …
  • Thank you for informing us about …
  • I am writing to express my concern about …

Feelings

  • I must admit I was disappointed to hear …
  • I was delighted to learn that …
  • I fully understand the need for …
  • I am concerned that …

Ideas

  • I would like to suggest that …
  • It would be highly beneficial to …
  • I would strongly recommend …
  • Perhaps you could consider …

Finish

  • I look forward to hearing from you.
  • Thank you for your attention.
  • Sincerely, / Best regards,
  • Full name
✓

Part 2 blueprint

🧱

Blog post / maqola rejasi — 4 paragraf, 180–200 so‘z

IntroductionRephrase the question + give your opinion clearly.
Body 1First reason / advantage + a real example.
Body 2Second reason or the other side + example.
ConclusionSum up and repeat your opinion in new words.

Task 1.2

Dear Manager,

Thank you for your email. Even I understand that the building needs some repairs and new equipment, I was a bit disappointed to hear that the fitness club will be closed for one month. I usually come a few times a week, so it’s an important part of my lifestyle.

I would like to suggest some improvements. The changing rooms are sometimes too small and not very clean, so maybe they can be repaired. It would be also nice to have more fitness classes in the evenings when most people can come.
Thank you for listening to our opinions. I hope to return to club soon.
Best regards,
Nicolas Tedros.

Guess the mark: ____ / 63/6👩‍🏫 Examiner:The response is on topic, but the questions are not fully addressed. The register is appropriate. A range of complex structures are used. Vocabulary is sufficient to discuss the topics. Errors in grammar, and word choice do not cause misunderstanding. Some cohesive devices and referencing are used to connect sentences.
Part 2

I think living in a small town is better than living in a big city, even if both have some advantages. In my opinion, small towns are more calm and people can live there with less stress. There is not so much noise and traffic like in big cities, so it’s easier to relax and enjoy free time. Also, the air is more clean and the nature is closer, which is good for health.

Another reason is that people in small towns usually know each other and are more friendly. There is a stronger feeling of community, and it’s easier to make friends. For example, in my town I often meet people I know when I go outside.

Of course, big cities offer more job opportunities and better education. You can find more shops, cinemas, and restaurants there. But I think life in a city can be very fast and tired. It’s not easy to find a silent place or to have time for yourself.

In conclusion, I prefer to living in a small town because the life is easier and more peaceful. I know that some people choose big cities, but for me, small town gives better quality of life.

EXERCISE1
Multilevel writing · Part 1 + Part 2

Library closure

📚
📍You are a member of a local community library. You received an email from the head librarian.
From: The Head Librarian · To: You · Email

Dear Member,

I hope this message finds you well. I regret to inform you that the library will be closed for two weeks starting next Friday for renovations and upgrades to our facilities. We aim to enhance your reading experience. In the meantime, we would love to hear your suggestions on what new programs or services we could offer upon reopening. Your input is invaluable to us.

Best regards,
The Head Librarian

Task 1.1Informal · B1
≈ 50 wordsWrite a letter to your friend, who is also a member of the library. Write about your feelings and what you think the library management should do about the situation. Write about 50 words.
Task 1.2Formal · B2
120–150 wordsWrite a letter to the head librarian. Write about your feelings and what you think the library management should do about the situation. Write about 120-150 words.
Part 2Blog post · C1
180–200 wordsYou are participating in an online discussion for language learners. “What are the advantages and disadvantages of online learning compared to traditional classroom learning?” Post your response, giving reasons and examples. Write 180-200 words.

Model answers

⭐

Namunaviy javoblar — belgilangan so‘zlarni o‘rganing

Task 1.1 · Informal

Hi Alex,
Can you believe the library's closing for two weeks for renovations? I'm a bit gutted as I just started a new book series! Honestly, it's inconvenient, but hopefully, the upgrades will be worth it.
Maybe we can try that new coffee shop during that time? Let me know what you think.
Best,
Alex

Task 1.2 · Formal

Dear Head Librarian,

Thank you for informing us about the upcoming renovations. While I understand the necessity for upgrades to enhance the member experience, I must admit to feeling a degree of disappointment regarding the two-week closure. As an avid reader, the library is a vital resource for me, and its temporary absence will present a challenge, particularly as I was looking forward to continuing with some current reading material.

However, I do appreciate the proactive approach to seeking member input for future programs and services. Upon reopening, I would strongly suggest considering initiatives such as expanding the digital collection, perhaps offering more e-books and audiobooks. Additionally, introducing workshops on digital literacy or author talks could be highly beneficial and popular among members. Ensuring clear communication about the reopening date and any new offerings will also be key to a smooth transition.

Thank you again for your commitment to improving the library.

Sincerely,
Alex

Part 2 · Model blog post

That's a really pertinent question. Having experienced both, I can see distinct advantages and disadvantages to online learning compared to traditional classroom settings.

1, flexibility is arguably the biggest benefit of online learning. You can often access materials and lectures at any time that suits your schedule, which is invaluable for those juggling work or other commitments. 2, I can rewatch a tricky grammar explanation as many times as needed, something impossible in a live class. 3, the sheer volume of resources available online, from interactive exercises to vast digital libraries, is often far greater than what a single classroom can offer.

4, traditional classrooms offer a unique social dynamic that online learning struggles to replicate. The face-to-face interaction with both the teacher and peers fosters immediate feedback and spontaneous discussion, which can significantly boost understanding and motivation. I've found that in-person group activities really help solidify vocabulary and speaking practice in a way that virtual breakout rooms sometimes don't quite capture. 5 direct, immediate human connection can sometimes lead to feelings of isolation for online learners.

6, I believe the ideal scenario might involve a blended approach, leveraging the convenience of online resources with the interactive benefits of in-person instruction.

EXERCISE2
Multilevel writing · Part 1 + Part 2

Community park

🌳
📍You are a resident in a neighborhood where a new community park is being planned. You received a flyer from the local council.
From: The Local Council Planning Department · To: You · Flyer

Dear Resident,

We are excited to announce plans for a new community park in our neighborhood! This project aims to create a green space for recreation and community gathering. We are currently in the early planning stages and want to gather your feedback on the proposed features. We have included a brief overview of some initial ideas, but we are keen to hear your thoughts and suggestions.

Your input is crucial in shaping this space for everyone to enjoy.

Sincerely,
The Local Council Planning Department

Task 1.2Formal · B2
120–150 wordsWrite an email to the Local Council Planning Department. Express your feelings about the park plans and provide specific suggestions for features or facilities you believe would benefit the community. Write about 120-150 words.
Part 2Blog post · C1
180–200 wordsYou are participating in an online discussion for language learners. “Is technology making our lives better or worse?” Post your response, giving reasons and examples. Write 180-200 words.

Part 2 · Model blog post

Technology is a highly debated topic, and I am of the opinion that its impact on our lives can be seen as both positive and negative.

1, technology has significantly improved our quality of life. 2, medical advancements have led to better healthcare outcomes, with telemedicine allowing patients to consult doctors remotely, especially during the pandemic. This accessibility is crucial for those in remote areas who might otherwise struggle to receive medical attention.

3, technology has transformed communication. Social media platforms enable us to stay connected with friends and family across the globe, fostering relationships that might have otherwise faded. 4, online learning has made education more accessible, allowing people from various backgrounds to acquire knowledge and skills that were previously out of reach.

5, there are downsides. The pervasive use of smartphones and social media can lead to social isolation and mental health issues, particularly among younger generations. Furthermore, the rapid pace of technological change can result in job displacement, as automation replaces traditional roles.

6, while technology has undoubtedly improved many aspects of our lives, it also poses challenges that we must navigate carefully. Balancing these benefits and drawbacks is essential for a better future.

Task 1.1 · Informal

Hi Jack,

Task 1.2 · Formal

Dear HR Department,

I am writing in response to your recent message regarding the initiative to enhance the welcome experience for new colleagues. I wholeheartedly support this plan; fostering a positive and inclusive onboarding process is crucial for employee retention and overall team morale.

I believe several elements could greatly contribute to making new staff feel comfortable and integrated quickly. Firstly, implementing a "buddy system" where an experienced employee is assigned to guide a new starter for their first few weeks could be invaluable. This buddy could answer informal questions, introduce them to others, and help them navigate company culture.

Secondly, a designated welcome lunch or coffee break within the first week, involving their immediate team, would provide a relaxed opportunity for introductions. Finally, ensuring that new employees have all necessary resources and access before their first day, and a clear introductory schedule for their first week, would significantly reduce initial stress and allow them to focus on learning their role and connecting with colleagues.

Thank you for prioritizing this important aspect of our workplace.

Sincerely,
Alex

Part 2 · Model blog post

The idea of celebrities as role models for young people is a bit of a mixed bag, in my opinion. While they certainly have influence, it's not always for the better.

1, some celebrities are genuinely positive influences. Many use their fame to support important causes, like raising awareness for environmental issues or promoting educational charities. 2, an actor who speaks out about the importance of literacy can inspire young people to value reading. 3, athletes who demonstrate dedication and discipline in their sport can motivate others to pursue their goals with hard work and commitment. These individuals often showcase admirable qualities like perseverance and resilience.

4, there are significant downsides too. The lifestyles portrayed by many celebrities can be extremely extravagant and sometimes promote unhealthy values, such as excessive consumerism or superficial appearances. This can create unrealistic expectations for young fans, leading to disappointment or a focus on material possessions. 5, some celebrities engage in controversial behaviour or scandals that are widely publicised, providing a poor example. Young people, especially, might not always have the maturity to critically assess the information they receive and could be negatively influenced by these aspects.

6, while celebrities can be role models, it's important for young people to be discerning and look beyond the glamour. They should focus on the actions and values that truly matter.

Part 2 · Model blog post

Social media has become an integral part of young people's lives, and I perceive that its impacts are both positive and negative. 1, social media platforms provide young users with opportunities for connection and communication. They can easily maintain friendships, share experiences, and engage with diverse communities around the world. 2, platforms like Instagram and TikTok allow users to express their creativity and showcase their talents, fostering a sense of belonging and self-identity.

3, the negative effects of social media cannot be overlooked. 4 is the impact on mental health. Young users often face pressure to present a perfect image online, leading to feelings of inadequacy and anxiety. Studies have shown that excessive use of social media can contribute to issues such as depression and low self-esteem. 5, exposure to cyberbullying is a serious problem that can have lasting emotional consequences.

6, while social media offers valuable opportunities for connection and creativity, it also poses risks to mental health and well-being. It is essential for young users to navigate these platforms mindfully, balancing their online interactions with real-world experiences to mitigate potential negative impacts.

In my opinion, both big cities and small towns have their unique advantages, but I believe that living in a big city offers more opportunities for personal and professional growth.

1, big cities are often hubs of diversity and culture. They provide access to a wide range of cultural experiences, including museums, theaters, and international cuisine. 2, in cities like New York or London, one can experience art from various cultures and attend performances from around the world. This cultural richness can greatly enhance one’s understanding of different perspectives.

3, big cities typically offer better job prospects. With numerous industries and companies located in urban areas, individuals have a greater chance of finding employment in their desired field. 4, someone interested in technology may find better opportunities in a city like San Francisco, which is known for its thriving tech scene.

5, it’s important to acknowledge the downsides of city living, such as higher costs of living and noise. In contrast, small towns often provide a sense of community and tranquility that can be appealing.

6, the choice depends on personal preferences and priorities, but for those seeking growth and adventure, big cities are often the better option.

Part 2 · Model blog post

Air pollution is a pressing issue that affects many cities around the world. I’m of the opinion that there’re several key reasons for this problem. Let’s look through some of them!

1, one of the main contributors to air pollution is industrial activity. Factories release a significant amount of harmful gases and particulate matter into the atmosphere during production processes. 2, in countries with heavy manufacturing industries, such as China and India, air quality often suffers due to emissions from factories.

3, transportation is another major factor. Vehicles, especially those that run on fossil fuels like petrol and diesel, emit carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides, and other pollutants. In urban areas with high traffic congestion, these emissions can lead to smog and respiratory issues for residents. 4, cities like Los Angeles and Mexico City frequently experience poor air quality due to the number of cars on the road.

5, household activities also contribute to air pollution. Burning wood or coal for heating and cooking releases smoke and toxic substances. In many developing countries, this practice is common and poses health risks to families.

6, industrial activities, transportation, and household practices are significant reasons for air pollution, and in my opinion, addressing these issues is crucial for improving air quality and public health.

This is a really serious and complex question: why is the crime rate among teenagers seemingly increasing? There isn't one simple answer, but I think several factors are contributing.

1 is the influence of social media and technology. Many young people are exposed to violent content online, which can normalize aggressive behavior. 2, some studies suggest that teenagers who play violent video games may become desensitized to violence and more likely to act out in real life.

3, socio-economic factors play a big role. Poverty, unstable home environments, and lack of parental supervision can create a breeding ground for crime. When families are struggling, or when children don't have consistent guidance, they are more vulnerable. 4, a teenager from a disadvantaged background might resort to theft out of desperation or a lack of other options.

5, some argue that mental health issues are also a contributing factor. Untreated depression, anxiety, or other challenges can manifest in destructive ways, including anti-social behaviour.

6, it's a multifaceted problem that needs a comprehensive approach, focusing on support, education, and opportunity.

Part 2 · Model blog post

The question of whether students should be allowed to use smartphones at school is a really hot topic with strong arguments on both sides. 1, I lean towards allowing them, but with clear guidelines and educational integration.

2, smartphones are undeniable distractions. When a student's phone is buzzing with notifications during a lesson, it's incredibly hard for them to focus on the teacher or the material. 3 decreased learning and poorer academic performance. We've all seen examples of students scrolling through social media or playing games instead of paying attention. This constant temptation can really hinder the educational environment.

4, smartphones are also incredibly powerful tools that can actually enhance learning. Many educational apps, online research tools, and even digital textbooks are accessible via smartphones. 5, a student could use their phone to quickly look up an unfamiliar word, access a relevant historical document for a project, or even use a language learning app during breaks. Banning them entirely removes these educational opportunities.

6, instead of an outright ban, I believe schools should focus on teaching responsible digital citizenship and integrating smartphones as learning aids. Setting clear rules, like phones being put away during direct instruction but allowed for specific research tasks, could be a good compromise.

Part 2 · Model blog post

This is a classic debate: should kids dive into a foreign language right when they start primary school, or is it better to wait until they reach secondary school? 1, but I personally believe that starting early offers significant advantages.

2 early language learning is that young children's brains are incredibly receptive to new sounds and structures. They are less inhibited and more willing to experiment with pronunciation, which is crucial for developing fluency. Think about how easily toddlers pick up their native language – this plasticity is a window of opportunity. 3, children who start learning a language like Spanish in primary school often develop a more natural accent and a deeper intuitive grasp of grammar compared to those who start years later.

4, I do acknowledge that starting too early without proper resources or engaging methods can be difficult. 5 to make early language learning fun and immersive, not a chore. This could involve songs, games, and interactive activities.

6, if primary schools can provide this kind of engaging environment, then starting early truly sets children up for greater success in the long run, providing them with a valuable skill for life.

Model answers

⭐

Namunaviy javoblar — belgilangan so‘zlarni o‘rganing

Task 1.1 · Informal

Dear Jack,
I hope you’re doing well! I just received an email from our internet provider's manager regarding the connection issues we’ve been facing. I feel relieved that they acknowledged the problem, but I think they need to improve their customer support and provide regular updates. It would really help us!
Best,
Alex

Task 1.2 · Formal

Dear Manager,

Thank you for your email and for acknowledging the ongoing internet connection issues in our area. While I appreciate the apology and your commitment to fixing them soon, I must admit I'm quite frustrated. For weeks now, my connection has been unreliable, frequently dropping during important video calls for work and causing significant disruption.

I believe the company should consider a few improvements. Firstly, enhancing the infrastructure would be crucial to ensure a stable connection for all customers. Additionally, providing timely updates about the status of repairs would help alleviate frustration and keep us informed. Lastly, improving customer support services would make it easier for users to report issues and receive assistance. Thank you for considering my suggestions. I look forward to seeing positive changes soon.

Sincerely,
Alex

Part 2 · Model blog post

This is a really interesting question for our discussion board: should schools prioritize practical life skills like managing money and cooking, or stick to the more traditional subjects like math and science? It's a tough balancing act, and I think a compromise is definitely needed.

1, subjects like math and science are fundamental. They build critical thinking, problem-solving abilities, and provide the foundational knowledge for many careers. Understanding physics or algebra 2 passing tests; it's about developing a logical mindset that's useful in many aspects of life. 3, a grasp of scientific principles helps us understand the world around us, from weather patterns to how our bodies work.

4, we can't ignore the importance of practical life skills. Many young adults leave school feeling unprepared for the realities of independent living. Knowing how to budget, manage personal finances, and prepare nutritious meals are essential skills that directly impact daily well-being and future success. I've seen friends struggle with debt because they never learned to budget, and others who rely heavily on convenience food because cooking seemed too daunting.

5, I believe schools should strive for a curriculum that integrates both. Balancing both traditional and practical subjects will 6 benefit students in their future endeavors.
